title: Behind on estimates? Your paycheck can catch you up
label: Deadline money moment

hook.text: Skipped estimates? Your *paycheck* can catch up.

lines: Dana has a day job and freelance clients.
The client money had no tax taken out.

beats.sub: counted as paid on each due date
beats.note: Even if it comes out of December paychecks.

items.l: extra withholding on the last paychecks

beats.text: Ask payroll how many *paychecks* are left.

cta.sub: We'll DM you our estimated tax guide.

captions.instagram:
Day job plus side income, and you skipped the estimated payments this year? Your paycheck can help you catch up.

✔️ The IRS treats federal tax withheld from your pay as paid in equal parts on each estimate due date, unless you show otherwise. Extra withholding in December counts toward the earlier dates too.
✔️ Give your employer a new Form W-4 with an extra amount per paycheck for the rest of the year.
✔️ Still short? The last 2026 estimated payment is due January 15, 2027.
✔️ Check how many paychecks are left before you pick the amount.

Source: IRS, Instructions for Form 2210; Estimated tax FAQ. General information, not advice for your situation.
